source_scope: Current validate_path_graph.py, shared build_path_graph.py, focused validator and builder tests, executor, followup contract and preflight were inspected directly. Bootstrap integration and affected migration/package/confinement callers also received a separate read-only same-model subagent review; no new external independence is claimed.

Each auditor run has immutable started/result records and a bounded log, with 30-second and 1048576-byte limits. Test sources were reviewed before execution; HTTP/Popen or synthetic application-dispatch guards remained active. Fixtures used owned tiny temporary files and canaries. No product source, actual configuration/index/model, personal document, network, GUI or credential operation was performed.
design/local-memory-v1-hardening/runs/f16-directory-hash-followup.v1.json was read as an additional disclosed residual. It is not silently incorporated as a new immutable source ID.

checks.reason: validate requires a caller-provided absolute source_root; missing or malformed authority fails without opening graph-selected source paths. The graph scope must exactly match that authority, and aliases are not silently resolved by the Validator. The observer rejects symlink roots/components without following them. The CLI requires --source-root. Independent focused runs on Python 3.14 and 3.9 passed the missing, wrong, relative and forged-scope authority checks under source-read guards, as well as alias rejection and real CLI parsing. Reads of the explicitly supplied graph/inventory input files are distinct from current-source traversal, as stated by the preflight contract.

Canonical relative-path checks reject absolute, parent-traversal, empty, dot, NUL and normalized-away spellings. Duplicate inventory paths remain errors rather than being accepted after dictionary overwrite. Duplicate JSON object keys are rejected by the decoder. Inventory kinds, integer metadata, observed status, source-hash form, graph schema/integrity, graph path/reference consistency and source path/locator checks gate current-source observation. Independent focused malformed-input and unsafe-path cases passed. Two added auditor cases additionally verified a rehashed forged node source path and a duplicate graph JSON key are rejected while source descriptor reads are forbidden. Malformed input exceptions are reduced to exception-type diagnostics rather than source contents.

After input checks, current-source observation uses the shared descriptor-bound observer and independently compares the full observed path set with the submitted inventory. It does not reopen graph-provided full source paths. New files or empty directories, missing files, source-byte changes and observer failures cause FAIL. The independent focused suites passed leaf/intermediate symlink replacement, post-stat replacement and same-inode mutation schedules with applicable outside-canary guards. The 19-case builder regression also passed with the previously repaired active-ancestor invalidation and descriptor cleanup assertions retained. Observer reuse is explicitly not independent algorithmic enumeration.

For the full current inventory, Validator compares kind, size, mtime, hash, read status and available birthtime; it separately checks each submitted node's source path/locator, type, raw source metadata and hash. Rehashing the enclosing JSON cannot bypass those current-observation comparisons. The recorded legacy diagnostic uses the old two-argument API and contains exactly two actual false-PASS failures: a newly added path and a forged node hash, plus one valid unchanged control. Its log hash 314a1825209f8dff656ae54e5fa491eff3d96d9da0b89f8a50941d809486cf4c matched executor evidence. The earlier missing-keyword baseline is not counted as multiple exploits. Current focused tests reject both defects. The auditor's additional same-size nested-file write with restored mtime failed specifically with current_source_sha256_changed and node_source_hash_mismatch, verifying full file-byte binding despite the separate root-digest residual.

Bootstrap passes the same selected source to the builder and to Validator's required --source-root argument; its existing run wrapper aborts the build on a failing Validator exit. The Reader resource contract now fingerprints actual Path builder and Validator bytes and sizes, and existing full contract comparison routes byte drift to reader_migration_required. The focused test checks both resource hashes against actual files, and migration tests add both Path code mutations while retaining prior assertions. The independent synthetic E2E and guarded migration/lineage suites each passed 15 cases, including a replay after the shared parser update. The two package callers were statically checked for explicit canonical roots and source-root arguments; their prior content/locator/security/original-byte assertions remain. Complete package/native execution was not performed.

The auditor independently completed focused 18-case suites on Python 3.14.6 and 3.9.6, the 19-case builder suite, 15-case synthetic E2E, 15-case guarded migration/lineage, and 3 additional adversarial cases. Every result was passed with zero skips/expected failures and exit 0; logs were below 3224 bytes and the longest supervised run was 1.593177 seconds. Runs 001 through 005 each had parser SHA-256 4429a50030143710786c0ee03a68f3d9243d555d121f832817a300824726a2c3 immediately before and after. After the independent parser task changed that dependency, runs 006 (E2E), 007 (migration) and 008 (adversarial) each had stable before/after SHA-256 73b9ad531d4e184b47636f0a7558e07cc44688d1499ddd666b8dc58610f830f7. No run spanned a detected parser change; 006/007 are the current integration replay. Their result hashes are 5a0423925c43b081d4b1bcbe158f2e622e75340f88670965bad339e7b4603ea6 and a1a5ceb9a67e2799a412c05c6a18c3dff41fa0e433183ba2fd2b283d50f9ba88; run 008 result hash is 533f937134bce26e5f1af48be7823d0c2e01e880157dd9843d7ea7c28b5b1614. Actual terminal log footers agreed with result counts, and all eight log hashes matched their metadata. All twelve required artifact-source hashes matched both the initial check and the post-run check. The dynamic parser hash is a separately recorded dependency, not an artifact-source freeze requirement or approval of F10.

The shared directory_hashes routine has a preexisting ordering defect: '.' and a top-level directory have equal slash counts, so lexical ordering computes the root before that directory digest exists. A nested same-length file-hash change can therefore leave the root digest unchanged. The disclosed pure-record reproduction was read and the ordering is confirmed in source. This is a nonblocking residual for the submitted Validator boundary because current verification also checks the complete path set and every inventory/file node hash; the added nested same-size byte-change test with restored mtime independently failed those checks. Neither this report nor the artifact establishes complete Merkle-root semantics or an independent directory-hash algorithm.
checks.required_action: Keep the disclosed directory-hash-order followup open. Separately add a bottom-up independent gold fixture and fix actual hierarchy-depth ordering after the current freeze; do not rely on the current root digest alone as complete tree-content attestation.

checks.reason: This pass approves the frozen Path Validator's external source authority, descriptor-bound current path/file observations, submitted node source binding, explicit bootstrap caller and Path-code generation fingerprint integration. It does not certify a global atomic snapshot, freshness after final checks, whole-tree resource bounds, all graph descriptive/summary/edge-policy fields, complete Merkle-root behavior, independent observer algorithms, actual model quality, native packaging, full application Python 3.9 support or whole-product acceptance. No source change or automatic rebuild was made by the auditor. Later source changes require their own stable evidence and approval; the disclosed nonblocking digest followup remains open.
